- Overestimate prices after strong positive sentiment spikes; model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently negative or neutral; model underreacts to bearish signals.
- Forecast tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially in upward trends; adjust for recent sentiment momentum.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed, model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecasts toward historical mean or sentiment-weighted trend.
- In high-sentiment environments, model often overcorrects after sharp moves; reduce forecast amplitude by 5–15% for sentiment > 0.6.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, model exhibits mean-reversion bias — overestimates peaks and underestimates troughs; apply downward bias to peaks and upward bias to troughs based on sentiment direction.
- If sentiment is trending upward for >5 days, model should not forecast a sharp drop unless sentiment reverses; avoid “sentiment reversal” overcorrection.
- When sentiment is low or negative, model often fails to anticipate sharp reversals; add a 1–2 day buffer for downside risk in low-sentiment periods.
